card: This pull request refactors validation and blockstorage methods to return error and flush status via util::Result and FlushResult instead of relying solely on AbortNode and shutdown triggers. Currently, validation code aborts without providing direct error details to callers, which forces libbitcoinkernel consumers to rely on asynchronous notification callbacks for fatal error handling. The author notes that propagating errors to callers makes kernel integration significantly easier without changing node runtime behavior. The PR depends on base PR 25665 for extended util::Result capabilities.
evidence: PR description: 'There are many validation functions that handle failures by calling AbortNode and triggering shutdowns, without returning error information to their callers. This makes error handling in libbitcoinkernel application code difficult, because the only way to handle these errors is to register for notification callbacks.'
problem: Many validation routines handle fatal conditions like disk write errors by calling AbortNode directly without returning error details to callers. For libbitcoinkernel embedders and decoupled application code, caller-level error recovery and inspection is difficult because errors can only be observed asynchronously through registered notification callbacks.
scope_notes: Large mechanical refactor across 55 files. It builds directly on #25665 for expanded util::Result functionality, introduces FlushResult types, and touches consensus validation, block storage, RPC handlers, and test fixtures to propagate results up the call stack.
summary: Refactors validation and blockstorage functions that can hit fatal errors to propagate error and flush details to callers via util::Result and FlushResult return types instead of relying solely on AbortNode shutdowns. Functions updated include block writes, state flushing, mempool package acceptance, snapshot activation, block connection, and chain activation. Function signatures across the call stack are updated with nodiscard annotations to ensure errors are checked or forwarded.
